verdicts.reviewer_notes: Second-round review, whole entry rechecked. Re-fetched https://www.cac.gov.cn/2026-09/14/c_1791137092283345.htm on 2026-10-07 (loads; read through a translating fetch tool). Verified against the page: title 《人工智能安全治理框架3.0》发布; page date 2026-09-14; released at the opening ceremony of the 2026 National Cybersecurity Publicity Week; released by the National Cybersecurity Standardisation Technical Committee (网安标委/TC260) under the guidance of the national cyberspace office (CAC), with CAC research and data-security centres and other institutions involved in drafting; keeps the core logic of risk classification, technical response and comprehensive governance; updates the risk classification and optimises the technical and governance measures relative to 1.0 (2024) and 2.0 (2025). The page has no statement on binding force and no effective date, so 'does not state that the framework is legally binding' is accurate. Every sentence in summary is supported. why_it_matters: first sentence now matches the round-1 wording and is supported. The second sentence ('practical effect depends on how later standards and enforcement draw on it') is a conditional inference, not a prediction stated as fact, and is framed as a consequence of the non-binding status; acceptable. event_date 2026-09-14 is the release date and matches the page (no separate adoption or effective date exists on the page). Stage in_force is the closest STAGES value for a released non-binding document; type guidance is consistent with a TC260 document. Source tier primary is correct (CAC is the guiding body and the publisher of the notice). Confidence was lowered to low as required in round 1, consistent with the rubric for machine-translated sources, and the summary explains why. Duplicate check: grep of content/items, content/instruments and content/digests (excluding runs) for 'safety governance', 'governance framework', 'TC260' and the source URL found only the unrelated Singapore agentic AI framework; existing China instruments are the labelling measures, cybersecurity law amendment and generative AI interim measures. Only one item in this file for the event. Round-1 required changes both applied. Minor, not blocking: accessed_at 2026-10-07T00:00:00Z looks like a placeholder midnight time rather than the actual fetch time.

Second-round review, whole entry rechecked against the same CAC page, re-fetched 2026-10-07. Name with Chinese title matches the page title. Summary: release date 14 September 2026, TC260 under CAC guidance, succession from 1.0 (2024) and 2.0 (2025), structure (risk classification, technical response, comprehensive governance), updated classification and adjusted measures are all supported. The researcher wrote 'The release notice does not state whether the framework is binding' instead of the round-1 suggested 'Non-binding framework...'. That is more accurate to the source, which is silent on binding force, so I accept the deviation. The internal process notes and the 'Status in_force is used loosely' sentence were removed; the remaining machine-translation caveat is reader-facing and appropriate. key_obligations now contain only the two structure-level statements the page supports, with no '(details not read)' wording. Timeline: single entry 2026-09-14, stage in_force, note matches the page (released at the opening of the 2026 National Cybersecurity Publicity Week), and source_url is the primary CAC notice. kind guidance fits the protocol definition (non-binding official guidance; no draft law). Status in_force is the least-bad STAGES value for a released guidance document. Not a duplicate: no existing instrument for any version of this framework in content/instruments. The item's instrument_slug matches this slug. last_verified is a valid UTC timestamp. Tone is neutral. Residual limit, already disclosed: the full framework text was not read, so key_obligations are deliberately high-level.
